==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|intreaty||obsolete}}

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:af|entreat|-y<id:abstract nouns>|text=+|tree=1}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ɪnˈtɹiːti/|/ənˈtɹiːti/|/ɛnˈtɹiːti/|a=UK}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-entreaty.wav|a=Southern England}}

* {{rhymes|en|iːti|s=3}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# The act of [[entreat]]ing or [[beseech]]ing; a strong [[petition]]; pressing [[solicitation]]; begging.
#* {{RQ:London Sea-Wolf|30|passage=She gathered many of the stones which I built into the walls of the hut; also, she turned a deaf ear to my '''entreaties''' when I begged her to desist. }}
#* '''1964''' October, P. F. Strawson, ''Intention and Convention in Speech Acts'', ''{{w|The Philosophical Review}}'', Volume 73, Number 4, [https://books.google.com.au/books?id=wBOrC7a240MC&pg=PA444&dq=%22entreaty%22%7C%22entreaties%22&hl=en&sa=X&redir_esc=y#v=onepage&q=%22entreaty%22%7C%22entreaties%22&f=false page 444],
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2002|author=N. P. Unni|title=Makers of Indian Literature: Amaruka|publisher=w:Sahitya Akademi|pageurl=https://books.google.com.au/books?id=LNzbG7fX3zQC&pg=PA32&dq=%22entreaty%22%7C%22entreaties%22&hl=en&sa=X&redir_esc=y#v=onepage&q=%22entreaty%22%7C%22entreaties%22&f=false|page=32
|passage=The '''entreaties''' of a lover and the rejection of the heroine lend charm to the stanza.}}
# {{lb|en|archaic}} A [[treatment]]; [[reception]]; [[entertainment]].
